# What's a Good Way to Manage Several Farms From One Dashboard?


A good way is to run every farm in the same connected structure, with a farm field on each record and permissions that filter each manager's default view, while the owner or head office sees a consolidated dashboard. On **Jestor** , this runs through shared **tables** with permission-based views.


Groups with several farms often end up with different spreadsheets and methods in each one. Comparing results is difficult, and the head office spends time collecting reports instead of supporting decisions.


## What separate farm systems cost


- Reports arriving late and in different formats
- No fair comparison between farms
- Duplicate work every time a new farm is added
- Best practices that stay inside one property
- Hours spent consolidating information


## How a multi-farm structure works


- Every record carries a **farm** field
- Permissions limit each manager's default view to their own farm
- The head office sees a dashboard with all farms combined
- Templates for checklists and records are shared


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Shared structure saves setup work for each new farm
- Comparisons between farms become fair
- Managers focus on their own property without losing the group's view
- This scales from two farms to a large agricultural group


Separate methods per farm One structure, filtered views


No consolidated picture Farm-level and group-level views


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can each farm manager see only their property?** Yes, permissions can filter the view by farm. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can the head office compare farms side by side?** Yes, a dashboard can rank or compare them.


**Do all farms need to use the same crops?** No, the structure supports different crops and activities.
